races.name: Betfred Tattenham Corner Stakes (Group 3) (Formerly The John Of Gaunt Stakes)

runners_data.name: Alcantor
runners_data.note: Hold-up specialist whose French Group 3 wins on testing ground perfectly suit this tactical scenario
runners_data.comment: Three Group 3 wins in France and may have needed the run on last month's stable debut
runners_data.spotlight: Front-runner who won three Group 3s in France for Andre Fabre (1m, testing ground) and was a very close fourth in the Group 1 Prix du Moulin at Longchamp (1m, good to soft) last September; below-par fourth on stable debut at Leopardstown (1m, good; Listed) four weeks ago but may have needed the run; of interest if rediscovering his best French form.

runners_data.name: Never So Brave
runners_data.note: Proven Group 1 performer whose hold-up style benefits from the likely conservative early pace
runners_data.comment: Pulled hard on comeback run at Sandown; leading claims on last August's Group 1 York win
runners_data.spotlight: Merely mid-division in the Group 1 QEII at Ascot (1m, good) last October and again below his best on reappearance at Sandown (1m, good) in April; however, he pulled hard last time and holds leading claims if rediscovering the form of his Group 1 City Of York win (7f, good to firm) last August; mixed messages in his form regarding the suitability of slow ground.

runners_data.name: Ten Bob Tony
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner who lost a shoe last time but needs to prove his consistency at this level
runners_data.comment: Disappointing last time but won this race last year (at its old home Haydock)
runners_data.spotlight: Inconsistent and he disappointed in Listed race at Haydock (7f, good) last time; however, he reportedly lost a shoe and prior to that was an encouraging fourth on his reappearance at the Curragh (7f, soft to heavy); won this race last year (good; at its old home Haydock) and posted fine third in Group 1 Foret at Longchamp (7f, very soft) last October; player if bouncing back.

runners_data.name: Chicago Critic
runners_data.note: Hold-up type returning from Dubai but hasn't shown his best form on recent home appearances
runners_data.comment: Short-headed in Meydan Group 2 in January but needs a bigger performance to take this
runners_data.spotlight: Short-headed in a Group 2 at Meydan (7f, good) in January but he needs a bigger performance if he's to take this and he hasn't been at the top of his game on his three starts since, most recently at the Curragh.

runners_data.name: Poet Master
runners_data.note: Lone front-runner who will control the race but may lack the finishing kick on 92 days break
runners_data.comment: Runner-up in two Group races last autumn; below best this term; e-w claims if back on song
runners_data.spotlight: Group 2 winner at the Curragh (7f, good) in July 2024 and runner-up in two 7f Group races last autumn (very soft/good); not at his best on his two runs this season but each-way claims if back on song today.

runners_data.name: Golden Mind
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with strong handicap form who handles testing ground and could benefit from any tempo increase
runners_data.comment: Better than ever in handicaps this season but has something to find today
runners_data.spotlight: 5yo who won three handicaps last year (including on heavy ground) and has been better than ever in such races this season, finishing second at Musselburgh (7f, good to soft) then fourth of 28 in the Victoria Cup at Ascot (7f, good); however, he has something to find against today's opponents.

runners_data.name: Witness Stand
runners_data.note: Class performer returning from 92-day break whose prominent style needs some pace to work with
runners_data.comment: Strong Group 2 form last summer; struggled since but perhaps a wind op will do the trick
runners_data.spotlight: Listed winner on soft ground who won the Group 2 Lennox Stakes at Goodwood (7f, good) last July before excellent second in the Group 2 Hungerford at Newbury (7f, good to firm) in August; he's lost his form on his last four starts but perhaps wind surgery will have done the trick; wears a first-time tongue-tie and capable of having a big say if rediscovering his best.

runners_data.name: Balmacara
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner with solid Listed form on soft ground but faces a significant class rise here
runners_data.comment: Has run well in defeat in Listed races but looks up against it in today's company
runners_data.spotlight: Listed runner-up at Sandown (1m, soft) last September and third in the same grade at Haydock (7f, good) four weeks ago on reappearance; however, he was comfortably beaten in that latest start and is 0-11 since winning novice contests at Doncaster in spring 2024 on second and third starts; up against it.

races.paceDynamic: Poet Master stands alone as the confirmed front-runner and will dictate proceedings unchallenged through steady fractions on the testing ground. Golden Mind and Witness Stand may track prominently but lack the pace to pressure the leader early. The lack of genuine pace will create a tactical affair with horses bunching into the straight, setting up a sustained finish up Epsom's undulating camber. This race shape strongly favors hold-up horses who can deliver one sustained run, as the modest early gallop will leave plenty in reserve for those coming from behind.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hold-up horses dominate
scenarios.trigger: If Poet Master sets conservative fractions and the field stays bunched
scenarios.body: The lack of early pace allows closers to conserve energy and unleash devastating late runs up the hill. Never So Brave and Alcantor benefit most from the tactical setup.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent racers strike
scenarios.trigger: If Golden Mind or Witness Stand apply early pressure to Poet Master
scenarios.body: The increased tempo stretches the field and favors those racing handy who can quicken off a stronger pace. Golden Mind's handicap progression and Witness Stand's class edge come to the fore.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front-runner survives
scenarios.trigger: If Poet Master gets completely uncontested fractions and kicks clear turning in
scenarios.body: The lack of early pressure allows the leader to save enough for a sustained drive to the line. Burke's 7f specialist proves too hard to peg back on the testing surface.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace collapse sprint
scenarios.trigger: If the tempo becomes absurdly slow and the race becomes a 2f dash
scenarios.body: The race turns into a pure speed test where class and finishing kick matter most. The highest-rated horses with natural pace have the edge in a bunched sprint finish.

watchPoints.text: Poet Master gets completely uncontested lead and steals a march turning for home before closers can organize
Never So Brave's fitness after 43-day break following disappointing Sandown reappearance
Witness Stand handling the return from 92 days off despite previous Group 2 success at this track
Golden Mind's ability to step up from handicap company to this Group 3 level
Track position and traffic problems developing in the straight with the bunched field scenario likely

races.name: Princess Elizabeth Stakes (Group 3) (Fillies & Mares) (Sponsored By Chapel Down)

runners_data.name: Sparks Fly
runners_data.note: Front-runner who should get an uncontested lead but faces stamina questions over this extended trip on testing ground
runners_data.comment: Third in this last year; won French Group 3 last autumn; creditable 4th at Chester latest
runners_data.spotlight: Four-time Listed winner who made Group 3 breakthrough at Saint-Cloud (1m, very soft) last October; ran well when 2l fourth in Group 2 Huxley Stakes at Chester (10.3f, good) four weeks ago; third in this last year and a penalty shouldn't prevent her being competitive again.

runners_data.name: Pacific Mission
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with class advantage but needs to prove effectiveness on this slower surface after firm ground struggles
runners_data.comment: Second in Group 2 and Grade 1 over 1m last year; may have needed return; player if at best
runners_data.spotlight: Runner-up in the Group 2 May Hill at Doncaster (1m, good to soft) and the Grade 1 Breeders' Cup Juvenile Fillies Turf at Del Mar (1m, firm) last autumn; below that level when fifth in 1m York Listed race on reappearance but it's possible she simply needed the outing; player if back to her best.

runners_data.name: Shes Perfect
runners_data.note: Consistent performer who races prominently and handles the going well but lacks a recent victory to boost confidence
runners_data.comment: Led for long way when third in Goodwood Listed on return and should be spot on now
runners_data.spotlight: All three runs last season were in France; suffered a heartbreaking demotion for connections when placed second in the French 1,000 Guineas at Longchamp (1m, good) and failed to stay an extended 1m2f in the Diane at Chantilly last June; not seen again until third in 1m Goodwood Listed event five weeks ago, fading late on as if the run was needed; should be spot on now.

runners_data.name: Princess Child
runners_data.note: Classic hold-up mare whose style suits the likely pace scenario but must overcome inconsistent 2024 form
runners_data.comment: Group 3 winner last year; second at same level this year but latest effort was below par
runners_data.spotlight: Group 3 winner at Tipperary (7.5f, yielding) at the end of last summer; matched that form when second in 1m Group 3 at the Curragh (soft/heavy) but needs to bounce back from a lesser effort at the Curragh last time.

runners_data.name: Breckenbrough
runners_data.note: French raider comfortable on soft ground who races prominently but faces significant class test in Group 3 company
runners_data.comment: Listed winner in France last autumn; creditable efforts in similar races there this spring
runners_data.spotlight: French raider who won a 1m Saint-Cloud Listed race on soft last autumn; arrives on the back of creditable in-frame efforts in similar races at Longchamp (7f/1m) this spring; often races prominently.

runners_data.name: Love Dynasty
runners_data.note: Lightly raced hold-up horse who handles soft/heavy conditions well but 70-day absence creates fitness concerns
runners_data.comment: Very lightly raced 5yo who has raced only on good or softer; drop back in trip is a help
runners_data.spotlight: Very lightly raced 5yo who left the impression 1m2f just stretched her when fourth in Nottingham Listed race on good-ground reappearance; raced only on soft/heavy prior to that, so won't be inconvenienced however much rain arrives.

runners_data.name: Pina Sonata
runners_data.note: Prominent racer returning from 70-day layoff whose recent Kempton AW form may not translate to turf conditions
runners_data.comment: AW Listed winner on reappearance and further progress is possible after only six starts
runners_data.spotlight: Came up well short in Group 1/Listed events in the second half of 2025 but different story on Kempton AW reappearance, readily seeing off ten rivals in 1m Listed race; winner on good to soft; capable of making her presence felt, with further progress a distinct possibility after only six starts.

runners_data.name: Arisaig
runners_data.note: Smart hold-up mare closely matched with main rivals but poor record at Listed/Group level raises questions about winning ability
runners_data.comment: Smart hold-up mare who is closely matched with Shes Perfect on latest Goodwood form
runners_data.spotlight: Smart hold-up mare who is closely matched with Shes Perfect on latest Goodwood Listed form over 1m on good; 0-6 at Listed/Group level but she's capable of a prominent showing if things fall right.

runners_data.name: Betty Clover
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer who finished behind key rivals last time and struggles to compete at this elevated level
runners_data.comment: Listed win at 2 but 0-13 since; held by Shes Perfect and Arisaig on latest Goodwood form
runners_data.spotlight: Won a Listed race at York (5f, good) as a 2yo but she's 0-13 since and finished behind Shes Perfect and Arisaig in a Goodwood Listed event last time.

races.paceDynamic: Sparks Fly will lead with Pacific Mission, Shes Perfect, Breckenbrough and Pina Sonata settling prominently behind her in the first half-mile. The sustainable pace will allow hold-up horses Princess Child, Love Dynasty, Arisaig and Betty Clover to track the field before making their moves. With only one confirmed front-runner and no pace pressure, the gallop will be steady through the middle sections before quickening significantly from two furlongs out on Epsom's testing undulations. This race shape strongly favours hold-up horses and closers who can produce their best efforts late, as the prominent runners will face a genuine stamina test in the final quarter-mile.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hold-up dominance prevails
scenarios.trigger: If Sparks Fly sets an honest but sustainable pace without early pressure
scenarios.body: The steady tempo allows closers to conserve energy before unleashing decisive finishing kicks. Princess Child and Arisaig benefit most from tracking the field and timing their runs perfectly on the unique Epsom gradients.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent horses control
scenarios.trigger: If Pacific Mission or Shes Perfect apply early pressure to Sparks Fly
scenarios.body: The increased pace stretches the field and prevents hold-up horses from closing effectively. Pacific Mission and Shes Perfect use their class and tactical speed to dominate from prominent positions throughout.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front-runner exploitation
scenarios.trigger: If Sparks Fly gets an uncontested lead and dictates fractions completely
scenarios.body: The lack of early pace allows her to conserve energy before quickening decisively when it matters. Sparks Fly capitalizes on her front-running style to build an unassailable advantage entering the home straight.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Late charge chaos
scenarios.trigger: If the pace becomes crawling slow through the middle sections
scenarios.body: A messy sprint finish develops where any horse can win regardless of running style. Love Dynasty and Betty Clover benefit from the tactical nature as class and finishing speed become paramount over positional advantage.

watchPoints.text: Sparks Fly could steal this if allowed to dictate fractions completely uncontested from the front
Pacific Mission's effectiveness on the slower ground remains questionable after previous soft surface struggles
Love Dynasty and Pina Sonata both return from 70-day breaks where fitness could be compromised
Princess Child's hold-up style perfectly suits the likely pace but her recent form consistency is concerning
Weather conditions could deteriorate further making the ground even more testing for speed horses

races.name: Coolmore Coronation Cup (Group 1)

runners_data.name: Jan Brueghel
runners_data.note: Natural front-runner who will dictate terms but faces the world's highest-rated horse unleashing a finishing kick behind him.
runners_data.comment: High-class horse who knuckled down the better to beat Calandagan in this race last year
runners_data.spotlight: High-class performer who has a record of 6-8 overall and 2-3 at Group 1 level, adding to his 2024 St Leger win when knuckling down the better to beat Calandagan in this contest (good to soft) 12 months ago; combination of cheekpieces and setting an unsuitably steady pace perhaps contributed to his King George defeat behind that rival; reappearance success in the Ormonde at Chester (1m5f, good) sets him up nicely for another Coronation Cup bid.

runners_data.name: Calandagan
runners_data.note: Supreme hold-up performer whose devastating turn of foot is perfectly suited to the likely controlled pace scenario.
runners_data.comment: Second in this race last year; has since become the world's highest-rated racehorse
runners_data.spotlight: Superstar gelding who has a record of 222211111 since racing at Group 1 level and is the highest-rated racehorse in the world; couldn't quite get past Jan Brueghel in this race last year but turned the tables in the King George and is on an impressive roll going into another rematch with that rival; prevailed at Meydan (Sheema Classic) last time despite the race not panning out ideally; duly strongly respected, assuming the ground is okay (not certain to run if it's a slog scenario).

runners_data.name: Bay City Roller
runners_data.note: Consistent prominent runner whose German Group 1 soft ground success gives him strong claims in these conditions.
runners_data.comment: Consistent but his Group 1 form is non-domestic; needs a personal best to win this race
runners_data.spotlight: Consistent colt whose Group 1 form is non-domestic, namely a success in Germany (1m4f, soft) last November and good second at the Curragh (10.5f, good) latest start; only a neck behind Lambourn on worse terms at Chester on reappearance, albeit with that rival rusty and likely to improve for the run, according to Ryan Moore; needs a personal best to land this prize.

runners_data.name: Lambourn
runners_data.note: Prominent racer who narrowly held off Bay City Roller at Chester but faces much stronger opposition stepping up in class.
runners_data.comment: Notable contender returned to the scene of his biggest moment, namely 2025 Derby win
runners_data.spotlight: Most wins on good ground but has form on soft; held on by only a neck from Bay City Roller on better terms in the Huxley (1m2f Group 2) at Chester on seasonal debut but proved game in first-time cheekpieces and, based on Ryan Moore's post-race comments, will come on for the run; notable contender in the retained headgear returned to the scene of his biggest moment, namely a clearcut success in last year's Derby (followed up in the Irish version).

runners_data.name: Convergent
runners_data.note: Progressive prominent runner whose penalty-defying Group 2 win shows he's still improving but needs gaps to appear.
runners_data.comment: Overcame trouble to win at Newbury on reappearance; progressive and adds great interest
runners_data.spotlight: Scored on soft ground on debut; flopped in the German race won by Bay City Roller but otherwise progressive and overcame trouble to defy a Group 2 penalty in Group 3 contest at Newbury (1m4f, good) on seasonal debut, taking record to 5-8; about 3l behind Lambourn at Chester last term but is now in the same ball park as that opponent on ratings, with a chance of further improvement to boot; adds great interest to this race.

runners_data.name: Illinois
runners_data.note: Staying specialist whose Cup race experience could prove valuable if this becomes a stamina test over Epsom's demanding contours.
runners_data.comment: One of three Ballydoyle runners; perhaps in here to set the pace and ensure a proper test
runners_data.spotlight: Runner-up in two Cup races last term; only a neck behind stablemate Jan Brueghel in the 2024 St Leger but was beaten about 5l by that opponent last month when bidding for a second success in the Ormonde at Chester, doing nothing to close their current ratings differential; perhaps in here to set the pace and ensure a proper test.

races.paceDynamic: Jan Brueghel will likely take up the early running with only genuine pacesetter in this small field, setting a measured gallop that won't be pressured early. The prominent runners Bay City Roller, Lambourn, Convergent and Illinois will track closely in behind, while Calandagan sits deeper looking to unleash his devastating finishing kick. With the pace sustainable rather than searching, the race will develop into a tactical affair where positioning into the straight becomes crucial. This controlled tempo clearly favours hold-up horses and strong finishers who can produce a sustained burst, with Calandagan's running style perfectly suited to exploit this race shape.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Calandagan's Sustained Drive
scenarios.trigger: If Jan Brueghel sets an even tempo without early pressure from the prominent group.
scenarios.body: The measured pace allows Calandagan to conserve energy before unleashing his world-class finishing kick, while the front-runners become sitting ducks. Barzalona can time his challenge perfectly as the highest-rated horse in the world demonstrates his class.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Duel Develops
scenarios.trigger: If Bay City Roller and Lambourn apply early pressure to Jan Brueghel through the middle sections.
scenarios.body: The increased tempo stretches the field and blunts Calandagan's finishing weapon, allowing the prominent racers to establish decisive positions. Jan Brueghel's stamina reserves prove crucial as he holds off the late challenges.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Convergent's Late Surge
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace becomes crawling and develops into a sprint finish from the home turn.
scenarios.body: Burke's charge benefits from his Group 2 penalty-defying form and ability to quicken sharply in slowly-run races. The tactical nature plays into his hands as he finds the gaps that matter when it counts.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Illinois Stays Strongest
scenarios.trigger: If the race becomes a true stamina test with a relentless gallop from halfway.
scenarios.body: O'Brien's staying specialist draws on his Cup race experience to outlast rivals in a gruelling finish. His proven stamina over extended trips gives him the edge when others weaken in the final furlong.

watchPoints.text: Calandagan getting a clear run at the two-furlong pole as any interference could cost him the race given his reliance on a smooth passage.
Jan Brueghel's ability to sustain his gallop down the hill as any weakening could allow the prominent group to establish race-winning positions.
Bay City Roller's positioning turning for home as Murphy needs to avoid getting trapped behind the leaders in this small field.
The pace through the middle sections as a crawling gallop would significantly alter the tactical complexion and suit different profiles.
Convergent finding racing room in the straight as he needs clear daylight to deploy his finishing kick effectively.

races.name: Betfred 'Dash' Handicap (Heritage Handicap)

runners_data.name: Vintage Clarets
runners_data.note: Hold-up style suits the strong pace perfectly and arrives 11lb lower than last year's fifth place finish
runners_data.comment: Prolific winner down the years; on a dangerous mark and revival isn't out of the question
runners_data.spotlight: Prolific winner down the years and he arrives off an 11lb lower mark than when fifth in this 12 months ago; yet to shine this year (poor draw at Chester on penultimate start) but it wouldn't be a huge shock to see him fare better today.

runners_data.name: Democracy Dilemma
runners_data.note: Front-runner who won at Haydock off this mark but faces two other confirmed pace-setters in a likely speed duel
runners_data.comment: Second here in 2024 off 3lb higher; has not found very best in 2026; needs a full revival
runners_data.spotlight: Front-runner; second in this race in 2024 off 3lb higher; ran away with a 5f handicap at Haydock (good ground) last September off this mark; unable to hit the same heights since but his AW third in February was a fair run; won't be inconvenienced should there be a marked deterioration in the going but a full revival is required; visor returns having been left off latest.

runners_data.name: Stormy Impact
runners_data.note: Hold-up specialist who won the 3yo Dash here last year and should benefit from expected strong gallop
runners_data.comment: Fast finish to peg back Lexington Blitz in 3yo Dash in 2025; can leave reappearance behind
runners_data.spotlight: In 2025 she took a big step forward from her seasonal return when sweeping through late to collar Lexington Blitz in the 3yo Dash on this card; also won at Wolverhampton in July (6f, AW) off 1lb higher than today; never a threat at York last month on return to action but it's not unreasonable to expect much better today and she is sure to get a strong pace to aim at.

runners_data.name: Kinswoman
runners_data.note: Progressive prominent racer but faces traffic dangers with 7 others wanting similar positions
runners_data.comment: Progressive in 2025 and reappearance was encouraging; up in weights but better to come
runners_data.spotlight: Progressive when dropped to 5f in the second half of 2025, winning a Windsor novice (good to firm) and adding handicap wins at Chester (good to firm) and Haydock (good); unable to justify odds-on favouritism at Yarmouth (5f, good to soft) 24 days ago on her return from seven months off but it was still a solid effort and she remains capable of better; another 3lb higher today but sure to be popular.

runners_data.name: Rhythm N Hooves
runners_data.note: Prominent style but gradually slipping down weights, needs less competitive affair than this
runners_data.comment: Handicapped to win soon but this race might prove a shade too competitive
runners_data.spotlight: Admirable campaigner who is gradually edging down the weights; type to pop up soon but perhaps in a slightly less competitive affair.

runners_data.name: Ziggy's Triton
runners_data.note: Prominent runner whose limitations exposed in stronger company, beaten only 3.5 lengths when seventh here last time
runners_data.comment: Musselburgh win in April came in Class 4; held in stronger company twice since
runners_data.spotlight: Saw off 11 rivals when scoring at Musselburgh in April (5f, good; Class 4) but he has had his limitations exposed in stronger company twice since; beaten only 3l at York two weeks ago but others are more appealing in today's field.

runners_data.name: King Of Light
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse returning from 36-day break, won off 6lb lower mark last September
runners_data.comment: Encouraging seasonal return at Goodwood; sharper today and the more rain the better
runners_data.spotlight: Won a 5f handicap (good to soft; first time in tongue-tie/cheekpieces combination) at Haydock last September off a 6lb lower mark; stayed on for second behind the impressive Lexington Blitz at Goodwood on last month's return; withdrawn at York two weeks ago having got upset in the stalls (9-1 at the time of withdrawal); the more rain the better; no accessories today.

runners_data.name: Dyonisos
runners_data.note: Yet to win for Ian Williams but hold-up style suits expected pace scenario perfectly
runners_data.comment: Second in two of his last three; not sure to confirm latest placing with Dream Composer
runners_data.spotlight: Yet to win for Ian Williams but he's down in the weights and has run well in two of his last three starts, pipped at Goodwood last month (5f, good); wouldn't be sure to confirm those placings with Dream Composer this time.

runners_data.name: Lexington Blitz
runners_data.note: Prominent racer gelded over winter, caught late in this race last year but has run well since return
runners_data.comment: Second at this meeting last year; impressed at Goodwood latest; up 9lb but on the upgrade
runners_data.spotlight: Picked off late in the 3yo Dash 12 months ago; gelded prior to his seasonal return and he has run well on both starts in 2026, following his close third at Musselburgh with an impressive win at Goodwood five weeks ago (5f, good); a 9lb rise asks a stiffer question but he is progressive.

runners_data.name: Dream Composer
runners_data.note: Won this race in 2024 off 5lb higher mark, hold-up style and Tony Carroll stable form both positive
runners_data.comment: Two good runs since joining Tony Carroll; won this race in 2024 off 5lb higher; big player
runners_data.spotlight: Trained by James Evans when winning this race in 2024 off a 5lb higher mark (good to soft); well beaten in it last year but he arrives in good form for his new stable, winning at Ripon in April and not enjoying the cleanest run when fourth at Goodwood 15 days ago; rain won't hurt his chance and he's of obvious interest.

runners_data.name: Emperor Spirit
runners_data.note: Prominent style rarely seen on slower than good ground, appreciated turf return at Ascot
runners_data.comment: Good 2nd at Ascot on last month's return to turf; rain would be a concern
runners_data.spotlight: Appreciated the return to turf when finishing second of 17 at Ascot five weeks ago; 1lb rise still leaves him on a feasible mark; rarely seen on slower than good.

runners_data.name: Betsen
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse fresh from Chepstow win 16 days ago but facing much deeper field today
runners_data.comment: Drop back to 5f saw him win a Class 4 at Chepstow last month; in much deeper today
runners_data.spotlight: 6f AW win on his stable debut in November; added to his tally when seeing off five rivals at Chepstow 16 days ago (Class 4; 5f, good to soft); in deeper today.

runners_data.name: Another Baar
runners_data.note: Front-runner returning from 107-day Bahrain stint, rattled off four-timer when last in form
runners_data.comment: Reeled off a four-timer last term; 5f win in Bahrain in January; looks high in weights
runners_data.spotlight: Acts on any ground; having dropped in the weights he enjoyed a revival last August/September, rattling off a four-timer (5f-5.3f); had a stint in Bahrain over the winter, unplaced on four occasions but recording a career best when winning a 5f event (good to firm) in January; looks on a tough mark back in Britain.

runners_data.name: Cindy Lou Who
runners_data.note: Prominent runner not in same form since progressive 2025 season ended
runners_data.comment: Bath 2nd on return was a fine effort but disappointing last time and now 11lb higher
runners_data.spotlight: Progressive in 2025 and she took her form to a new level when second of 14 in a Bath Listed event on her reappearance (5f, good); not in the same form at Newbury (6f, good) when last seen seven weeks ago and she is now 11lb higher; others look stronger.

runners_data.name: Eclairage
runners_data.note: Prominent racer better on AW than turf, wasn't beaten far in Dundalk Group 3 last time
runners_data.comment: Speedy front-runner; fine second at Navan 3 weeks ago; 8lb higher but foolish to discount
runners_data.spotlight: All four wins have come on the AW at Dundalk and she wasn't beaten far in a Group 3 there on her final run in 2025; fully effective on turf and ran a cracker at Navan three weeks ago, showing her trademark early speed before being picked off late on (front two pulled 6l clear); 8lb higher today but this track should play to her strengths; chance.

runners_data.name: Almaty Star
runners_data.note: Front-runner hit with 8lb rise after Yarmouth win, better on AW than turf historically
runners_data.comment: Better on AW; in a much deeper race than the one he won at Yarmouth eight weeks ago
runners_data.spotlight: Better on AW than turf but took advantage of a good opportunity at Yarmouth in April (5f, good); hit with an 8lb rise for that, bringing his turf and AW marks into line; blew the start back at Yarmouth last month but the stewards deemed him a non-runner due to having his head turned as the stalls opened; risky on the back of that and there are other pace influences to contend with today.

runners_data.name: Arklow Lad
runners_data.note: Prominent style with cheekpieces, solid York run three weeks ago suggests readiness
runners_data.comment: 2-4 for Mick Appleby; solid effort at York last month; one to consider
runners_data.spotlight: 2-4 since joining Mick Appleby, notably a Class 2 handicap win at Pontefract (5f, good to soft; cheekpieces first time) in April; solid run at York three weeks ago and one for whom rain would be no concern.

runners_data.name: Star Chorus
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse slowly away at Goodwood with blindfold removed late, looks vulnerable to smart start needed
runners_data.comment: Two AW wins this winter; slowly away at Goodwood latest; vulnerable at this level
runners_data.spotlight: In good form on AW for Mike Murphy this winter, winning twice at Southwell (5f/6f); slowly away (blindfold removed late) at Goodwood two weeks ago; looks vulnerable at this level and goes without accessories this time.

runners_data.name: Rogue Enforcer
runners_data.note: Prominent runner suited by good ground or slower, finished down field in two recent handicaps
runners_data.comment: Listed win in Italy last October; well held at big prices in two starts for his new stable
runners_data.spotlight: Suited by good ground or slower; won a 5f Listed race in Italy on his final start for a French yard; big prices and finished down the field in two 5f handicaps last month; dropped 7lb for his troubles but he arrives with a point to prove.

runners_data.name: Brazen Bolt
runners_data.note: Veteran prominent runner won big-field handicaps at York and Goodwood last July but aging profile concerning
runners_data.comment: Two solid efforts this year and 1-1 at Epsom; suited by good/firmer
runners_data.spotlight: Won big-field 5f handicaps at York and Goodwood last July; two solid efforts in defeat this season and he won on his only visit to Epsom, albeit over 7f; not impossibly treated but he wouldn't want the ground to be any slower than good.

races.paceDynamic: Democracy Dilemma, Another Baar and Almaty Star will ensure a strong gallop from the outset, with all three confirmed front-runners unlikely to give each other an easy time. The 8 prominent racers including Kinswoman, Rhythm N Hooves, Ziggy's Triton and Lexington Blitz will create dangerous congestion behind the leaders, particularly problematic 2-3 furlongs out on this downhill track. With stamina certain to be tested by the pace and traffic issues likely for those needing room, this race shape strongly favours hold-up horses who can stay wide and finish fast. The tactical advantage lies decisively with the patient back-markers.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Strong Pace Suits Closers
scenarios.trigger: If Democracy Dilemma and Another Baar duel early and the prominent brigade gets tangled up
scenarios.body: The pace will be unsustainable and create gaps for the hold-up horses to exploit wide and late. Patient riders staying out of trouble will have decisive advantages as the pace-setters weaken.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses Early
scenarios.trigger: If the three leaders settle more than expected and don't go hard enough early
scenarios.body: The race will become a sprint finish where prominent racers can position perfectly without stamina concerns. Those with tactical speed from good positions will dominate the finish.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Traffic Chaos Benefits Wide
scenarios.trigger: If the 8 prominent runners cause a wall of horses and block the rail
scenarios.body: Hold-up horses forced wide will have clear runs while others get shuffled back in the pack. The widest drawn closers with room to manoeuvre will have unimpeded passages to victory.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Front-Runner Survives
scenarios.trigger: If one of the leaders gets an uncontested lead while the others are held up
scenarios.body: Democracy Dilemma or Another Baar could steal a march and have enough left to resist the late challenge. The lack of early pressure would preserve stamina for the business end.

watchPoints.text: Democracy Dilemma and Another Baar will likely engage in early speed duel that could set up perfect scenario for closers
Watch for traffic problems 2-3 furlongs out when 8 prominent runners converge in limited space on downhill track
Stormy Impact won this 3yo version last year and hold-up style perfectly suits expected strong gallop
Vintage Clarets arrives 11lb lower than last year's fifth place and gets ideal pace setup for late charge
Star Chorus was slowly away last time when blindfold removed late, needs sharp start to avoid traffic issues

races.name: Betfred Derby (Group 1) (No Geldings)

runners_data.name: Rebel Rocker
runners_data.note: Hold-up specialist who improved dramatically when stepped up in trip, 39 days since last run could be freshness advantage
runners_data.comment: 2nd in the Listed Trial here; shapes as if 1m4f will suit him well but faces a stiff task
runners_data.spotlight: Strong late on to grab a maiden at Kempton (1m, AW) in November and came from last to second in the six-runner Listed Trial here (1m2f, good; 33-1) in April; hopes for the latter form seem to have been punctured and although he looks capable of better and shapes as if 1m4f will suit him well, 1m4f in something other than the Derby would seem much more realistic.

runners_data.name: Benvenuto Cellini
runners_data.note: Proven front runner with Group race wins, Ryan Moore booking significant, handles good to soft conditions well
runners_data.comment: Stays well, good form; something to prove on soft/heavy, otherwise bold show looks assured
runners_data.spotlight: Frankel colt who was dominant in a maiden last July, a Group 2 at Leopardstown (1m) in September and Group 3 Chester Vase (12.5f, good) one month ago; his free-flowing, long-striding action was seen to good effect in those races, but not on heavy ground when third in the Group 1 Futurity at Doncaster (1m) in October; soft ground would also introduce something for him to prove but otherwise he brings strength of stamina and among the best form; if the ground is okay, a bold show looks assured.

runners_data.name: Action
runners_data.note: Carries head high which may hinder stamina, closely related to Derby winner but needs to settle better
runners_data.comment: 2nd in 2yo Group 1 (heavy) and to Item in Dante; carries head high and cheekpieces go on
runners_data.spotlight: Closely related to 2025 Derby winner Lambourn; carries his head high but ended last season with a close, battling second in the Group 1 Futurity at Doncaster (1m, heavy) and front-running second in the Dante at York (10.2f, good) last month was of a similar order, albeit no match for Item in the final 1f; a disappointing, sluggish display on reappearance was his only start with tongue tied; likely to stay 1m4f, with a possible place role but it's unlikely to be more unless the new cheekpieces have a major positive effect.

runners_data.name: Item
runners_data.note: Confirmed pace-setter but has only raced up to 1m, stamina at 1m4f completely unproven
runners_data.comment: Settling a bit better would help but he won going away in Group 2 Dante at York (10.2f)
runners_data.spotlight: Well on top last September in a maiden at Kempton (7f, AW) and novice at Bath (1m, good to firm); non-runner in Group 1 Futurity due to heavy going; not the easiest to settle when reappearing in Group 2 Dante at York (10.2f, good; 11-2) last month but he mastered front-running Action in the last half furlong to win it well, putting Christmas Day in the shade as well; settling a bit better (fine as 2yo) would cement claims for 1m4f but this son of Frankel won going away and brings clear potential, plus leading form and an unbeaten record.

runners_data.name: Pierre Bonnard
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with excellent Group 1 form, Soumillon knows Epsom well, strong recent form
runners_data.comment: Looked every inch a serious Derby contender as 2yo and that impression still holds sway
runners_data.spotlight: Asserted late on to finish firmly on top last October in a Group 3 at Newmarket (good to firm) and Group 1 Criterium de Saint-Cloud (very soft) and they were over 1m2f; 3yo campaign got off to a muted start but he briefly hit the front in Derby Trial at Leopardstown before James J Braddock swooped and Aidan O'Brien has stressed that he went gently with him at home until after that race; his sire and dam's sire were Derby winners (dam won 1m2f Group 1 Nassau) and he now moves up from 1m2f; he looked every inch a serious Derby contender last term and that's probably still the impression to go with.

runners_data.name: James J Braddock
runners_data.note: Versatile prominent runner, won on heavy going as juvenile, 27 days break ideal preparation
runners_data.comment: Swooped on Pierre Bonnard in the 1m2f Leopardstown Derby Trial and 1m4f will suit him well
runners_data.spotlight: Second start as 2yo was a 6l win in Curragh maiden (1m, heavy); never able to challenge on return in the Group 3 Ballysax won by Christmas Day and couldn't have left it any later in the Derby Trial back over Leopardstown's 1m2f (good) four weeks ago, but upstaging Pierre Bonnard so dramatically in the latter reinforces the feeling that 1m4f will suit him well; his sire's sole Group 1 win was at this trip; each-way player for trainer and jockey who won the Oaks yesterday.

runners_data.name: Christmas Day
runners_data.note: Progressive type improving with each run, won Dante third time out, handles testing conditions
runners_data.comment: Put in his place by Item in the Dante at York, albeit plugging on as if 1m4f could help
runners_data.spotlight: Maiden success was on heavy going; Group 3 Ballysax at Leopardstown (1m2f, good to yielding) on April reappearance made it three wins in a row and his Dante third at York (10.2f, good) next time was at least as good on form; while lacking anything like the same dash as winner Item at York, and also unable to get to grips with stablemate Action, he did plug on as if 1m4f could help; it clearly needs to.

runners_data.name: Balzac
runners_data.note: Another pace-setter who may struggle with sustained gallop, stamina questions at this trip
runners_data.comment: Lingfield Derby Trial 3rd but Maltese Cross and Bay Of Brilliance were just over 6l ahead
runners_data.spotlight: Novice winner whose rallying third of six in Listed race here (1m2f, good) in April suggested that longer trips would suit; tried 11.6f in the Lingfield Derby Trial (good to firm) and recorded his highest rating, but Maltese Cross and Bay Of Brilliance were just over 6l ahead of him; major work to do.

runners_data.name: Maltese Cross
runners_data.note: Classic hold-up horse who thrives off strong pace, Haggas stable in excellent form
runners_data.comment: Won his last three; pedigree and performance are all about 1m4f; firmly in the e-w picture
runners_data.spotlight: Debut was on soft; all four of his races were tight finishes and he won the last three; pulled it out of the fire against useful rivals in a valuable novice event at Newbury (1m2f, good) and narrowly maintained an advantage over Bay Of Brilliance as the pair drew clear in a ding-dong battle for the Lingfield Derby Trial (11.6f, good to firm) four weeks ago; his pedigree is all about 1m4f, including with his sire and dam's sire both Derby winners, and he also shapes as if every yard today will suit; needs to pull out more again but has to be in each-way calculations.

runners_data.name: Alderman
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner returning from 49-day break, likely needs this run for fitness
runners_data.comment: Promising, scopey sort from famous middle-distance family but he's been running in maidens
runners_data.spotlight: Travelled well and challenged from the rear at Newbury (1m3f, good; 17-2) on reappearance seven weeks ago, sticking to his task manfully too while chasing home an exciting prospect at a respectful distance; a promising, scopey sort from a famous middle-distance family but his progressive form in maidens, without a win, does not make him a serious Derby contender.

runners_data.name: Bay Of Brilliance
runners_data.note: Front runner who has made all recently, will contribute to fierce early pace
runners_data.comment: Pushed Maltese Cross all the way in the Lingfield Derby Trial (11.6f) on reappearance
runners_data.spotlight: Half-brother to smart Flat and hurdle winner Absurde; odds-on winner of a maiden at Goodwood (1m2f, soft) and novice at Redcar (1m1f, good to soft; made all) on last two starts as 2yo; pushed Maltese Cross all the way in Lingfield Derby Trial (11.6f, good to firm) and could improve on that first-time-out display; more to do but he's heading the right way.

runners_data.name: Ancient Egypt
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with tactical speed, Frankel breeding suggests stamina will be there
runners_data.comment: 1m4f beckons strongly after Newmarket Listed win, putting him in each-way calculations
runners_data.spotlight: Frankel colt bought for 1,100,000gns as a yearling; all four races on good to firm; Beverley and Goodwood novice wins last summer before the Group 2 Royal Lodge saw a comprehensive end to his unbeaten record; he returned to Newmarket, however, with an ultimately authoritative win in a five-runner Listed race (1m2f) five weeks ago, helping to make the running; 1m4f beckons strongly after that and he's included in each-way calculations.

runners_data.name: A Taste Of Glory
runners_data.note: Inconsistent front runner who faded badly in Group 1 company last time
runners_data.comment: 33-1, subsided rapidly to be last of six in Lingfield Derby Trial (11.6f, good to firm)
runners_data.spotlight: Won a Brighton maiden and 1m2f AW handicap at Lingfield; however, he ended last season with last of ten in a French Group 1 (1m2f, very soft) and subsided rapidly to be last of six in the Lingfield Derby Trial (11.6f, good to firm; 33-1); his owner is renowned for Derby contenders who have run well at big prices, but hopes for this one may be stretching it.

runners_data.name: Poker
runners_data.note: Expensive purchase but limited form, another pace-setter likely to struggle late
runners_data.comment: Front-running second of four in a 1m4f Haydock novice in April, so has a mountain to climb
runners_data.spotlight: Having fetched 4,300,000gns in 2024, he is the most expensive yearling colt ever sold at auction in Europe; by Wootton Bassett out of a sister to Oaks winner Was; on the other hand, he was left nearly 9l behind by Bay Of Brilliance at Redcar (1m1f, good to soft) in October and sported cheekpieces at 10-1 when a front-running second of four to a stablemate in Haydock novice (1m4f, good to firm) in April; admirably tenacious in the latter but the dream was once of so much more.

races.paceDynamic: Item, Action, Benvenuto Cellini, Balzac, Bay Of Brilliance, A Taste Of Glory and Poker will create a relentless gallop from the start over Epsom's unique undulations. With seven confirmed front runners in a 14-runner Derby field, the pace will be fierce early and sustained throughout, particularly testing as they climb from Tattenham Corner. The good to soft ground will add further stamina demands to an already punishing test. This red-hot pace scenario strongly favours hold-up horses and prominent racers with proven stamina reserves who can strike late.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Sustained Pace Battle
scenarios.trigger: If the seven front runners maintain their aggressive styles and create the expected strong gallop
scenarios.body: The relentless tempo will find out the front runners' stamina limitations in the final two furlongs, setting up perfectly for closers. Hold-up specialists like Maltese Cross and Rebel Rocker will benefit most from the collapse ahead.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Early
scenarios.trigger: If several front runners drop out of contention before halfway due to the fierce early gallop
scenarios.body: The race will become tactical in the middle stages before accelerating again, suiting versatile prominent racers. Those with tactical speed and finishing kick will dominate the final outcome.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front Runner Survives
scenarios.trigger: If one of the classier pace-setters like Benvenuto Cellini or Action gets first run and sustains their effort
scenarios.body: The winner will come from those who can travel strongly in the first three and kick clear before the closers arrive. Early positioning becomes crucial with less time for back markers to make up ground.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Tactical Crawl
scenarios.trigger: If the front runners surprisingly check each other's pace in the early stages creating a slow tempo
scenarios.body: The race becomes a sprint finish where pure speed matters more than stamina, completely changing the complexion. This unlikely scenario would favour those with the best turn of foot regardless of position.

Rebel Rocker's 39-day absence means watch for fitness, but his late kick could be devastating if pace collapses
Bay Of Brilliance making all in recent wins but faces much stronger pace pressure here than previously encountered
Christmas Day's progressive profile means watch market support as indication of stable confidence in stamina lasting

races.name: Cherryfield (Croydon) Lester Piggott Handicap (GBBPlus Race)

runners_data.name: Allegresse
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with strong finishing kick but untested in truly-run handicaps and returning after 36-day break
runners_data.comment: Limitations on last two starts; handicap debut; stamina in family suggests he should stay
runners_data.spotlight: Won from the front in two Kempton novices (1m, AW); weakened out of it in a Group 3 at Newmarket (1m2f) on final 2yo run and mastered by his three rivals late on in a conditions stakes at Goodwood (1m, good; unraced on softer) on reappearance, so he does not present the most glittering case for this handicap debut, but stamina in family suggests he should stay.

runners_data.name: Starlight Time
runners_data.note: Natural front runner making seasonal debut after 212 days off which raises serious fitness concerns
runners_data.comment: 2-3 as 2yo; 1m2f plausible and he should bring potential to this seasonal/handicap debut
runners_data.spotlight: Won a small-field maiden here (7f, good) last July on debut; well held in eighth of 26 in a valuable sales race at Newmarket (7f, good) but he was on his own through the final 1f when making most to win at 1-2 in a novice at Chelmsford (1m, AW) in November; 1m2f is plausible and he should bring potential to this seasonal and handicap debut.

runners_data.name: Savvy Disko
runners_data.note: Prominent type who can track early pace but may lack the finishing punch for this competitive level
runners_data.comment: Won Lingfield novice (1m, AW) last month, always close up and leading in final strides
runners_data.spotlight: Minor honours at Newmarket (7f, good) in October on first two starts; 7-1 for 12-runner novice at Lingfield (1m, AW; York Tower third) last month and always close up to win by a neck; getting up in the final strides there boosts hope for 1m2f (despite pedigree) and he's a promising newcomer to handicaps.

runners_data.name: Hell Yeah He Did
runners_data.note: Front runner who acts on soft ground with stamina proven, benefits from gelding operation and suits tactical demands
runners_data.comment: Will be suited by 1m2f+ and nothing to prove if ground is testing; seasonal/handicap debut
runners_data.spotlight: All three turf races as 2yo were on soft or heavy, making most and rallying stoutly to win a maiden at Nottingham (1m) on final outing; gelded since; seemingly no doubt that he will still be suited by 1m2f+ and nothing to prove if the ground is testing; one to note on seasonal/handicap debut.

runners_data.name: Lake Como
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with untested soft ground credentials but strong recent AW form suggests improving trajectory
runners_data.comment: Has not transferred best AW form to two 1m turf handicaps; worth a go at this new trip
runners_data.spotlight: Unraced on softer than good; found serious improvement over 7f/1m on AW but, although running respectably, he's not transferred the best of that form to 1m turf handicaps on last two outings; worth a go at this new trip.

runners_data.name: Tailgunner Joe
runners_data.note: Closer who showed Dubai form over middle distances, needs to bounce back from poor Newcastle effort 52 days ago
runners_data.comment: Needs to rebound from a poor show (1m2f) in April and he was gelded the following day
runners_data.spotlight: Better in Meydan campaign in December-March, including a 1m win and he shaped as if he stayed 1m1f on final start there; needs to rebound from a poor show at Newmarket (1m2f) in April and he was gelded the next day.

runners_data.name: York Tower
runners_data.note: Front runner stepping up in trip with 7lb weight advantage, lacks proven stamina for this demanding test
runners_data.comment: Handicap newcomer; plenty suggests that 1m2f+ will suit and best days are ahead of him
runners_data.spotlight: Second over 7f at Yarmouth (good) and Chelmsford (AW) on his only two starts as 2yo; respectable third to Savvy Disko in novice at Lingfield (1m, AW) on return last month; handicap newcomer, with plenty to suggest that 1m2f+ will suit and best days are ahead of him.

runners_data.name: Folk Pageant
runners_data.note: Natural leader with recent 1m2f win and proven soft ground form, racing off just 7-day turnaround
runners_data.comment: Saw it out well when winning 1m2f handicaps at Newmarket and Chester on last two starts
runners_data.spotlight: Second on good to soft on her only 2yo start; last of nine on handicap debut at Southwell (1m, AW) in April but won her other three starts this season, in 1m2f handicaps at Newmarket and Chester on last two occasions; 6lb rise is a sterner reaction since latest start but she's seen those last two races out strongly and could have more to give; major player.

runners_data.name: Pendella
runners_data.note: Front runner who shaped like non-stayer over 1m4f but showed improved stamina over 1m2f at York
runners_data.comment: Reeled in late in the day when second of ten at York (1m2f, good) last time; raised 2lb
runners_data.spotlight: Shaped like a non-stayer over 1m4f at York on turf debut in May, but reeled in only late in the day when second of ten there over 1m2f (again good ground; raised 2lb today) nine days later; ridden by Jack Nicholls last time and that performance puts her on the shortlist.

runners_data.name: Silver State
runners_data.note: Consistent front runner with soft ground win and regular partnership with 5lb claimer Rose Dawes
runners_data.comment: Needs to resume improvement after helping to set strong pace in bid for 1m turf hat-trick
runners_data.spotlight: Usually ridden by Rose Dawes; won four of seven handicaps, all once visored, including from the front over 1m at Bath (good to soft) and Doncaster when returned to turf; helped to set a strong gallop when fifth of ten at Haydock latest but he needs to resume improvement and this new trip is not sure to help.

runners_data.name: Be The Standard
runners_data.note: Lead type unproven on testing ground, disappointed as favorite last time and may lack stamina reserves
runners_data.comment: Both handicap performances left plenty to be desired; back in trip for this second 3yo run
runners_data.spotlight: Unraced on softer than good; flopped when favourite for five-runner nursery at Newcastle (1m, AW) in October and weakened into fifth of eight at Chester (1m4f; 5-1) on return, so his two handicap performances left plenty to be desired; back in trip today and perhaps he needed that latest run.

races.paceDynamic: Seven confirmed front runners including Starlight Time, Hell Yeah He Did, York Tower, Folk Pageant, Pendella, Silver State and Be The Standard will ensure a strong gallop from the start. This aggressive early pace will stretch the field and create a demanding test of stamina over the 1m2f trip on soft ground. The relentless tempo will favor hold-up horses like Lake Como and Tailgunner Joe who can conserve energy and finish strongly. This race shape strongly favors closers and stamina types who can capitalize on the inevitable pace collapse in the final two furlongs.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Strong Pace Collapse
scenarios.trigger: If the seven front runners engage in a fierce early battle through testing ground
scenarios.body: The breakneck gallop will deplete the leaders and create perfect conditions for late-running types to sweep past exhausted pace-setters. Hold-up horses with tactical speed will have every chance to time their challenges perfectly.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Tactical Front Runner Wins
scenarios.trigger: If one of the pace-setters can secure an uncontested lead while others battle behind
scenarios.body: A smart front runner like Hell Yeah He Did or Silver State could steal crucial lengths early and maintain just enough to resist late challenges on ground that suits stamina. The soft conditions will aid their cause by slowing closing sectionals.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Mid-Division Sweeper Prevails
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is steady enough for prominent racers to conserve energy while staying in touch
scenarios.body: Horses like Allegresse and Savvy Disko positioned in third or fourth can avoid the early pace battle while remaining close enough to strike. Their superior class can tell in a sustained drive from two furlongs out.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Sustains Throughout
scenarios.trigger: If the soft ground prevents a complete pace collapse and maintains even sectionals
scenarios.body: The front runners manage their effort better than expected and the race becomes a test of pure stamina from the two-furlong pole. This scenario heavily favors proven stayers with tactical pace.

watchPoints.text: Hell Yeah He Did and Silver State must break cleanly to secure early positions before the pace battle intensifies
Lake Como needs to settle kindly in rear given his hold-up style and unproven soft ground credentials
Starlight Time's 212-day absence makes him vulnerable if the pace becomes genuinely searching from the outset
Folk Pageant racing on quick 7-day turnaround after recent 1m2f win could impact recovery on testing ground
Tailgunner Joe requires strong early positioning from David Egan to utilize his proven finishing kick effectively

races.name: HKJC World Pool Northern Dancer Handicap (GBBPlus Race)

runners_data.name: Prydwen
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with strong recent form but carries top weight of 135lbs which may prove telling in a competitive handicap
runners_data.comment: Edging up the weights again but has won off higher and won't mind how the ground is riding
runners_data.spotlight: Prolific 8yo who gained his 11th success when taking 1m4f Ripon handicap (good) in April; got a 2lb nudge after that and received a further 3lb rise after finishing fifth in 2m Group 2 in Germany four weeks ago; while that's not ideal, he's won off higher marks and won't mind how the ground is riding.

runners_data.name: Dancing In Paris
runners_data.note: Hold-up specialist returning after 273 days absence but has excellent course form and handles the going conditions
runners_data.comment: No win last term but ran some fine races; returns over a trip probably short of his best
runners_data.spotlight: He hasn't won since August 2024 but ran some fine races in defeat last season, including when second of 14 at Glorious Goodwood (1m6f, good to soft) in August; those efforts have ensured his mark is holding up, however, and he makes his comeback over a trip probably short of his best these days.

runners_data.name: Give It To Me Oj
runners_data.note: Can make running or sit prominent, proven on soft ground with strong recent form including course and distance success
runners_data.comment: Dual C&D winner; recent run over 2m should have teed him up nicely for this; considered
runners_data.spotlight: Acts on soft; can make the running; won six (four over hurdles, two on Flat) of seven starts in a golden spell last February-October, including over C&D in September in both the Jump Jockeys Derby (soft) and Apprentices' Derby (good); recent run over 2m at Goodwood should have teed him up nicely for what could be a plan from last year's winning yard; considered.

runners_data.name: Regal Ulixes
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer who won on soft as a 2-year-old but faces traffic issues from his style in this large field
runners_data.comment: Various excuses last three starts and looks like this trip is worth a go again; respected
runners_data.spotlight: Won on soft (1m) as a 2yo; gelded after just two starts last year (included 1m2f win) and he scored off 5lb lower on AW in February; various excuses in three subsequent outings when he frequently looked as though this step back up in trip is well worth another go; respected.

runners_data.name: Lord Melbourne
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with excellent Epsom record including wins at this trip, particularly effective on soft ground
runners_data.comment: 2-3 here but poor this year; tempting mark if he can stage a revival; market check needed
runners_data.spotlight: Won 23-runner November Handicap (1m4f, soft) in 2024 and he's 2-3 here (1m2f and 1m4f) including a win on good to soft last September; those are the clear positives but he's been poor in three starts at 1m2f (snow/AW/good) this year; has a tempting mark if he can stage a revival, so needs a market check.

runners_data.name: Spinning Wheel
runners_data.note: Prominent type with improving profile who made all at Leicester on similar ground last time out
runners_data.comment: Boasts 3-6 record; unexposed and looks a big contender to build on his encouraging return
runners_data.spotlight: Unraced as a juvenile but now boasts 3-6 record, winning his first two and back on the scoresheet when making all at Leicester (1m4f, good to soft) in October; bumped into a quite well-regarded sort when second at Goodwood (1m6f, good) a fortnight ago and this unexposed 4yo looks a big contender to build on that encouraging return.

runners_data.name: Asgard's Captain
runners_data.note: Hold-up specialist and course regular who finished third in this race last year on good to soft
runners_data.comment: Goes well here and won at Newmarket latest; career-high mark but unlikely to be far away
runners_data.spotlight: Track regular who finished third in this race (good to soft) in 2024 and stayed on from the rear to be fourth in last year's edition; also won last season's Great Metropolitan over C&D (good) and got back in the winning groove when taking Newmarket handicap three weeks ago; latter success puts him on a career-high mark but he's unlikely to be far away.

runners_data.name: Too Soon
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner from the in-form Moore yard but frustrating record of 1-14 despite being well-regarded
runners_data.comment: Sole win came here (8.5f, heavy); cheekpieces go on and he may be capable of a big run

races.paceDynamic: Antrim and Gordon Grey are confirmed front runners who will contest the early lead, with Give It To Me Oj also capable of pressing from a prominent position. This creates an honest gallop over the 1m4f trip on good to soft ground, though neither leader has blistering early speed so the pace won't be suicidal. With a large field of 17 runners and most adopting hold-up tactics, the early pace will be solid but sustainable. This race shape favours prominent runners and those with tactical speed who can position handily, as the hold-up horses will face a traffic nightmare in the straight.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Sustained Gallop Benefits
scenarios.trigger: If Antrim and Gordon Grey maintain a solid but not excessive early pace
scenarios.body: The honest tempo allows prominent runners to stay in touch without over-racing, while the large field creates congestion problems for hold-up horses coming from the rear. Those positioned within the first six turning for home will have a crucial advantage.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runners Collapse
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace becomes too strong between Antrim and Gordon Grey
scenarios.body: Both leaders tire in the final two furlongs after an overly contested first mile, allowing late-running hold-up specialists to sweep past a faltering field. The good to soft ground aids stamina types who can produce sustained finishing kicks.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Traffic Chaos Favours Rail
scenarios.trigger: If the large field bunches up turning into the straight creating severe crowding
scenarios.body: Horses drawn low and positioned on the rail avoid the worst traffic problems while those in mid-pack struggle to find racing room. Early positioned runners who secure good positions have a clear passage to the line.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Uncontested Leader Dominates
scenarios.trigger: If one of Antrim or Gordon Grey gets an uncontested lead while the other fades early
scenarios.body: The surviving pace-setter gets first run on the field and proves hard to peg back, especially with Gordon Grey's excellent course record providing confidence. The honest pace leaves enough in reserve for a strong finish.

races.paceDynamic: Partisan Hero is the lone confirmed front runner and will set an uncontested lead from the gate, allowing him to dictate terms at his own pace. Apollo One, Gold Star Hero, Sondad, Solar Aclaim, Eye Of Dubai, Twilight Jet and Topwarrior will settle prominently but none are aggressive early pacers, creating a moderate tempo through the first half. The lack of early pressure means the pace will be sustainable rather than searching, setting up a finish where stamina and acceleration from off the pace become crucial. This scenario strongly favours hold-up horses who can produce late kicks, as the pace-setters will have plenty left for the finish.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Uncontested Leader Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Partisan Hero gets an easy lead and the pace stays moderate throughout
scenarios.body: The front runner conserves energy early and has enough left to resist late challenges on ground he's unproven on. His recent York win shows he's found his best form over sprints and the lack of early pace pressure plays to his strengths.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Late Kick Prevails
scenarios.trigger: If the moderate early pace allows closers to wind up with devastating finishing speed
scenarios.body: The patient hold-up horses get the perfect setup as the leaders go too slowly early, leaving them vulnerable to strong finishing kicks. Fine Interview and Roman Dragon have the class to exploit this tactical advantage despite their different profiles.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Stalkers Strike
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent runners can position perfectly and kick before the hold-up horses get organized
scenarios.body: Gold Star Hero and Sondad use their tactical speed to get first run on the leaders while the back markers are still getting organized. Their prominent positions allow them to strike at the crucial moment when the pace quickens.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Shock
scenarios.trigger: If Partisan Hero stops quickly and the prominent group fails to capitalize immediately
scenarios.body: The uncontested leader hits the wall dramatically and the prominent pack hesitates, allowing a rank outsider to sneak through. Twilight Jet's recent winning form or Topwarrior's fresh legs after a long break could catch everyone napping.
